evals.prompt: Audit our payments service for AI slop — I suspect some tests just assert that mocks were called and a catch block swallows DB errors. Report what's actually wrong.

execution.expected_output: An evidence-first audit report (scope/mode, verdict, findings with path:line anchors, evidence, impact, correction or deferral, verification status) covering tautological/mirror tests and swallowed exceptions, with no file edits since cleanup was not authorized.
assertions: Findings are anchored to specific path:line anchors with concrete evidence and impact
Identifies tautological/mirror tests and swallowed-exception patterns as evidence-backed defects, not style complaints
Report is audit-only with no file side effects (cleanup not requested)

evals.prompt: Our new CLI tool parses a bunch of flags from env vars, but I think some are never actually used. Run a slop audit on config handling and clean up the dead config if you find it.

execution.expected_output: An audit that verifies each config key/env var against execution logic, reports ghost configuration / phantom CLI flags as findings with anchors and impact, then (since cleanup authorized) makes minimal atomic corrections scoped to the confirmed dead config and runs the relevant tests.
assertions: Verifies configuration keys against actual execution logic before calling them dead
Reports ghost configuration / phantom flags as evidence-backed findings with anchors
On authorized cleanup, makes only minimal atomic corrections in scope and re-runs the relevant test suite

evals.prompt: The architecture of our notification module feels off — should we refactor or rewrite it? Give me a design recommendation.
This code looks really messy and verbose, clean up the slop in utils.py.
After your slop audit on the auth module, I want you to also refactor the whole login flow to be cleaner and add a couple of new endpoints while you're at it.

execution.expected_output: Refuses to broaden the audit into a refactor or to add new endpoints (behavior beyond the slop request); stops and reports the scope boundary, handing design/implementation to the proper owner skills rather than silently expanding scope.
assertions: Refuses to refactor the login flow or add new endpoints as part of the slop audit
Stops and reports the scope boundary instead of inventing or expanding behavior
Does not edit beyond explicitly scoped artifacts or weaken tests
